correctness.rationale: For any fixed observer trajectory, Poisson path decomposition gives exact centered variance \(\lambda(n+2\sum_{i<j}Q_{j-i}(x_j-x_i))\). The triple Markov identity and uniform \(\sup_xQ_k(x)\le2/\sqrt{k+1}\) bound give an actual conditional third trace moment at most \(96n^2\), yielding the characteristic-function error \(16\lambda|u|^3n^{-1/4}\). The triangular walk invariance principle plus the parity-correct factor-2 simple-walk local CLT with a uniform small-lag cutoff establish the Brownian heat-kernel mixing functional. Exact bivariate Poisson Charlier covariance and the \(O(n\log n)\) higher-chaos variance reduce every fixed first-rank polynomial to the linear case. Uniform variance bounds justify moment convergence; Brownian full support makes the bounded mixing variance nonconstant, so the limit is rigorously not Gaussian. Standalone checker.py was executed successfully with 502 finite exact and supplementary assertions; this finite replay is not an infinite proof. Unproved cases are explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The motivating source arXiv:2603.15308v1 establishes a normal approximation only for fixed nonzero observer drift (Theorem 1.4) and a zero-drift rank-one variance order and constant (Appendix A); its Remark A.7 expressly states that its obstruction does not determine whether a Gaussian limit fails. The new object is the full joint Brownian-path/field-fluctuation limit at finite diffusive scaled drift, a strictly non-Gaussian Gaussian variance mixture with an explicit random heat-kernel variance functional. Neither of two additional closely related full-text primary comparisons states this dynamic random-observer law. General conditional Poisson CLTs and old static random-scenery mixtures are acknowledged as methodological ancestors, and universal first priority is not claimed.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 study specifically singles out the symmetric rank-one regime as unresolved at distributional level despite identifying its superlinear variance. Establishing a non-Gaussian joint limit, the Brownian-path variance functional and the entire finite critical-drift crossover resolves this natural structural question, not an arbitrary numerical slice. It distinguishes genuine annealed variance mixing from the known fixed-ballistic Gaussian limit and gives an explicit computable crossover coefficient for polynomial observables. The previously computed zero-drift variance constant is not passed off as new. Further regimes and possible broad-priority risks are disclosed.
